growth_stages.name: Dormancy / Pre-Sprout
growth_stages.description: Not a named stage in the source ruleset (which begins its stage list at 21 DAP with Sprouting & Emergence) -- added here to cover days 0-20 so growth_stages has no gap at the start of the cycle. The mother sett/seed yam sustains the plant during this window, which is also why the fertilizer rule below has a hard floor at 30 DAP: too early and the crop is not yet drawing on soil nutrients.

growth_stages.name: Sprouting & Emergence
growth_stages.description: Shoot emergence from the seed yam/sett.

growth_stages.name: Vine Growth & Canopy
growth_stages.description: Vine elongation; this is the window in which staking should occur to maximise light capture and reduce leaf disease.

growth_stages.name: Tuber Initiation & Bulking
growth_stages.description: Underground tuber forms and bulks with starch.

growth_stages.name: Maturity / Senescence
growth_stages.description: Vines yellow and die back, signalling harvest readiness.

operations.name: Seed Yam Selection & Treatment
operations.description: Selection of healthy, medium-sized whole seed yams or cut setts; cut surfaces treated with wood ash or an approved fungicide against rot before planting.

operations.name: Land Preparation (Mounding/Ridging)
operations.description: Large mounds or ridges formed on deep, well-drained soil to allow tubers to expand freely. The source ruleset does not separate a distinct land-clearing step for this crop the way this knowledge base's other files do -- kept as a single operation to stay faithful to the source document rather than imposing an unstated split.

operations.name: Planting
operations.description: Seed yams/setts planted into mounds, spacing approximately 1m x 1m (~10,000 stands/ha). Recommended early in the season for a full bulking window.

operations.name: Staking
operations.description: Lifting vines onto stakes to maximise light capture and reduce leaf disease.

operations.name: Fertilizer Application (NPK)
operations.description: NPK application. Too early and the crop is still living off the mother sett, not the soil; too late and it has passed the window where fertilizer meaningfully supports bulking.

operations.name: Weeding & Mulching
operations.description: Regular weeding plus mulching of mounds to conserve moisture and suppress weeds. The source ruleset gives no specific day-window for this operation (unlike staking and fertilizer, which both have explicit DAP thresholds), so no timing validation_rule is attached to it here -- flagged as a gap in the source document, not an oversight.

operations.name: Harvest
operations.description: Harvest after vines yellow and die back.

operations.name: Curing & Storage
operations.description: Curing and storage in a ventilated yam barn; roots handled gently to avoid bruising, which triggers storage rot.

validation_rules.condition: Hard block if staking is logged before planting -- there are no vines to stake yet.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 6 (Yam), Stage 3.

validation_rules.condition: Flag after 60 DAP. Recommended window is lifting vines onto stakes by 4-8 weeks after planting; staking logged later than that is still physically possible but has lost most of its light-capture/disease-reduction benefit.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 6 (Yam), Stage 3.

validation_rules.condition: Hard block before 30 DAP -- the crop is still living off the mother sett and has not yet developed the root system to use applied fertilizer.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 6 (Yam), Stage 3.

validation_rules.condition: Flag after 90 DAP. Recommended window is application by 4-8 weeks after planting; applied later than 90 days, the crop has moved well into tuber bulking and the fertilizer is less useful.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 6 (Yam), Stage 3.

validation_rules.condition: Hard block before 150 DAP -- tubers have not meaningfully bulked before this. Note: the source ruleset states this floor but does NOT state a corresponding hard-block ceiling for lateness (unlike the yield-typo ceilings, which are always given). Delayed harvest past 270 DAP is documented only as a warning-level in-ground rot/nematode risk, not a hard block, and no upper block is invented here that the source document does not itself specify.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 6 (Yam), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: Flag before 180 DAP. This sits above the 150-day hard-block floor: harvest logged between 150 and 180 days is physically accepted but flagged, since the typical window given for this crop starts at 180 DAP.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 6 (Yam), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: Flag after 270 DAP, due to in-ground rot and nematode damage risk from extended in-soil storage.
validation_rules.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 6 (Yam), Stage 4.

validation_rules.condition: Harvest can only be logged once per planting cycle for this template. Same simplification and caveat as this knowledge base's other root/tuber crop files: real-world piecemeal lifting is common practice but not yet supported by the workflow engine.
validation_rules.source: Inherited convention from cassava.json / ofsp.json -- not separately addressed in the source ruleset for this crop.

validation_rules.condition: Global rule: no operation may be logged with a date earlier than the previous operation's logged date for the same farm/cycle (no backdating that would reorder the sequence).
validation_rules.source: Inherited convention across this knowledge base -- corresponds to the ruleset's Anti-Fraud & Anti-Typo Controls section (GPS Polygon Anchor Rule / data-integrity intent), not a crop-specific rule.

soil_requirements.drainage: well-drained, deep soil (needed for unrestricted tuber expansion)

weather_preferences.notes: Not covered numerically in the source ruleset section for this crop -- rainfall and temperature figures here are carried over from general West African yam agronomy references as a placeholder, and should be replaced with ruleset-sourced figures if/when the document is extended to cover this. Flagged for agronomist review.

diseases.name: Yam Anthracnose (Colletotrichum gloeosporioides)
diseases.symptoms: Leaf spotting and vine dieback, most damaging on unstaked/poorly aerated vines.
diseases.management: Timely staking (see staking operation) improves airflow and light, directly reducing this disease's severity; resistant varieties where available.
diseases.source: Not itself detailed in the source ruleset's Yam section -- inferred from the ruleset's own stated rationale for staking ('reduce leaf disease'), which implies a specific disease risk without naming one; anthracnose is the disease most commonly cited elsewhere in West African yam literature as the target of that staking benefit. Flagged for agronomist confirmation against the source ruleset's intent.

pests.name: Yam Nematodes (Scutellonema bradys / Meloidogyne spp.)
pests.symptoms: Internal tuber damage (dry rot), often not visible externally until storage; explicitly named in the source ruleset as a reason to avoid delaying harvest past 270 DAP.
pests.management: Harvest within the recommended 180-270 DAP window (see yam_r_harvest_late_warn), clean planting material, field rotation.
pests.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 6 (Yam), Stage 4 (named directly as 'nematode damage').

yield_model.expected_yield_per_hectare: 8.15 (Nigeria national average, FAO 2024 estimate); normal range 5.0 - 12.23
yield_model.notes: Range taken directly from the source ruleset's stated Pass tier. Earlier expected yield, kept as the record of what was replaced: 5.0 - 20.0.

tiers.message: Must be logged as a Disaster/Loss Event.
Improbable -- likely data-entry error or inflated plot size.

yield_validation.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 6 (Yam), Yield Validation table. NOTE: the source table as written has an unaddressed gap -- it states Pass as '5.0-20.0 t/ha' and Soft Warning as '>25.0 t/ha', leaving 20.0-25.0 covered by neither tier. This crop file's yield_validator.py raises an error (does not silently pass) for any value matching zero tiers, so transcribing the gap as-is would make a real 22 t/ha harvest crash the validator rather than just being mis-flagged. Resolved here by extending Pass to 5.0-25.0, i.e. treating the document's '>25.0' threshold as the literal, operative boundary and '20.0' as the rounder figure mentioned in the same breath rather than a second real threshold. Flagged for agronomist/ruleset-author confirmation that this resolution matches intent.

version_history.changed_by: AgTrail Knowledge Base - new crop, Medium-priority tier, built from Master Ruleset
version_history.summary: Initial file for Yam (White Yam, Dioscorea rotundata), first of the 8 Medium-priority crops from the AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset not yet in this knowledge base. Unlike vitamin_a_maize.json, ofsp.json, and cowpea.json (which were built from general web research since no equivalent internal document existed yet for those crops), this file is built directly from Section 6 of the Master Ruleset docx, which is the platform's own authoritative source -- so nearly every operation, timing rule, and yield tier here is a direct transcription rather than independently sourced research. Three points where the source document itself was incomplete or ambiguous were resolved rather than silently papered over: (1) growth_stages in the source begins at 21 DAP (Sprouting & Emergence) with no stage covering days 0-20; added a 'dormancy_presprout' stage to cover it, explicitly marked as not from the source. (2) weeding_mulching has no stated DAP window in the source (unlike staking and fertilizer, which both have explicit thresholds), so no timing validation_rule was invented for it. (3) The yield_validation table has a genuine gap between the stated Pass ceiling (20.0 t/ha) and the Soft Warning floor (25.0 t/ha) -- transcribing it as-is would let engine.yield_validator.validate_yield() raise an error on a plausible real yield (e.g. 22 t/ha) instead of returning a result. Resolved by extending Pass to 5.0-25.0; flagged for confirmation against the ruleset author's actual intent. Also did not invent a hard-block harvest-lateness ceiling, since the source explicitly treats extended in-ground storage as a warning-level (nematode/rot) risk, not a hard block -- unlike this knowledge base's other crop files, which added their own anti-typo ceilings independently. Not yet agronomist-reviewed against the ruleset author's intent for the three flagged resolutions above.
version_history.source: AgTrail Master Agronomist & Validator Ruleset, Agrolinking Solutions Ltd., July 2026, Section 6 (Yam).

version_history.summary: The high end of the harvest estimate range was 16.3 t/ha (capped at twice the typical yield). Per CEO decision on 28 Oct 2026 it is now capped at 1.5 times the typical yield, 12.23 t/ha. The yield checks are unchanged; the ruleset best case stays as ruleset_high.

harvest_estimate.method: Typical is the FAO national average for Nigeria in 2024. The low end is the crop's normal low from the yield checks (the CEO's ruleset). The high end is that ruleset's best case, capped at 1.5 times the typical yield, so it stays close to what farms really get (CEO decision, 28 Oct 2026; it was twice the typical yield from 25 to 28 Oct). The harvest window is the expected window in the crop's timing rules, where they give one. The range is what is normal for a farm, not a forecast for this one.
caveats: National averages hide the spread between farms, so a single farm can be well outside the typical figure.
FAO flags the 2024 figure for this crop as its own estimate (flag E), not a figure reported by Nigeria. It is weaker evidence than the figures for maize or soybean.
Not a prediction for this farm: it does not know this season's rain, soil, seed or care.
The high end is capped at 1.5 times the typical yield (12.23 t/ha). The ruleset's own best case is 25.0 t/ha, which a well-run farm can reach but few farms do.
The FAO figure for yam is an FAO estimate for 2024; only the older yam figures (2019 and before) were reported by Nigeria itself.
